metadata.title: CAFR C6 Ramp Detection vs C3 Preemption Diagnosis

CF0_W120_Baseline.policy: Production Priority (C5 > C1 > C4 > C2 > C3 > C6 > C7)

CF1_Priority_Swap_C6_over_C3.policy: Priority Swap (C5 > C1 > C4 > C2 > C6 > C3 > C7)

CF2_C3_Deferral_Gate.policy: 2-Check Deferral on C3 when C6 is incubating

CF3_Margin_Tie_Break.policy: Confidence Margin Tie-Break when C3 and C6 fire

conclusion.defensible_conclusion: C6 recall (26/120, 21.7%) under W_c6_base=120 is limited by two primary mechanisms: (1) unfulfilled C6 detection criteria due to short post-ramp observation / stability veto (50 SKUs, 41.7%), and (2) ramp preemption by competing causes (44 SKUs, 36.7%), led by C3 (24 SKUs, 20.0%) and C2/C7 (17 SKUs, 14.2%). Counterfactual evaluation reveals: (a) Simple priority swap (CF-1: C6 > C3) recovers +7 C6 detections (to 33/120, 27.5%) with zero C0 FP impact, while losing 2 genuine C3 detections. (b) A 2-check C3 ramp deferral gate (CF-2) recovers +13 C6 detections (to 39/120, 32.5%) by giving incubating C6 transitions time to mature, but sacrifices 5 true C3 detections (dropping C3 recall from 11 to 6). (c) Margin arbitration (CF-3) does not recover C6 because C3 occurrence margin consistently exceeds C6 stability margin. Crucially, even with deferral, maximum C6 recall remains capped at ~32.5% because 50/120 series never produce a stable, sustained cell transition in the available post-ramp horizon.
